cases.prompt: $doctoral-field-training Create a Chinese HTML tutorial for reinforcement learning in /tmp/rl-doctoral-tutorial. I know machine learning and PyTorch, can spend 10 hours per week for six months, and want to develop research judgment.
expected_behaviors: Treats reinforcement learning history as a causal problem genealogy
Plans the complete table of contents but generates only the first review-paper-style chapter
Writes the tutorial site into the exact requested folder
Generates index.html, assets/styles.css, data/tutorial.json, and data/learning-state.json
Asks the learner to read Chapter 1 in HTML and explicitly acknowledge completion before Chapter 2 is generated

cases.prompt: Create a doctoral review-paper collection about databases by reconstructing their technical history: which problems produced each data model, why previous approaches failed, what evidence drove adoption, and which research questions remain.
expected_behaviors: Recognizes the request as doctoral field training
Accepts database systems as a legitimate research direction
Asks for the output folder before producing content
Does not substitute a pasted chat lesson or standalone outline for the incremental HTML textbook

cases.prompt: Create an offline HTML tutorial that trains me to doctoral-level competence in compiler optimization through the field's technical history.
expected_behaviors: Asks for the output folder before writing files
Does not silently choose a destination
Retains the technical-history and review-article requirements

cases.prompt: $doctoral-field-training Generate a complete doctoral HTML review collection for causal inference in /tmp/causal-inference-doctoral and verify every exact citation.
expected_behaviors: Uses available research tools before treating exact citations as authoritative
Labels citation confidence according to the skill rules
Includes predecessor, turning-point, critical, and synthesis works
Produces Chapter 1 in HTML and waits for reading acknowledgement before later chapter bodies

cases.prompt: I want to become a frontend engineer. Build me a learning path that will make me an expert.
expected_behaviors: Explicitly rejects frontend engineer as the terminal doctoral field rather than producing a framework or job-skills roadmap
Offers two to four recognized choices such as human-computer interaction or browser and web-platform systems
Explains each choice through its research object, questions, methods, practice, and recognized communities or venues
Asks the learner to choose and does not select, rank, or recommend a candidate on their behalf
Does not build the curriculum before the learner chooses
forbidden_behaviors: Invents and selects a hybrid field such as interactive Web systems engineering
Continues into a weekly curriculum, literature cluster, exercise, or mastery gate
Offers a React, tooling, project-delivery, interview, or crash-course roadmap

cases.prompt: 我想速成一名前端工程师，请给我安排一个 React、组件库和面试题的学习路线。
expected_behaviors: Rejects the proposed job-skills framing while preserving the learner's underlying ambition
Does not produce a React bootcamp, interview-preparation plan, or generic frontend checklist
Provides several recognized choices such as human-computer interaction or browser and web-platform systems instead of asking the learner to invent candidates
Explains the academic or industrial research basis and research practice of every choice
Waits for the learner's explicit selection before producing a curriculum or HTML artifact
forbidden_behaviors: Chooses a field for the learner
Creates an 8-week or other time-boxed engineering syllabus
Treats employability, interview performance, or a portfolio project as the terminal outcome

cases.prompt: $doctoral-field-training I choose browser and Web-platform systems. Build a complete Chinese doctoral tutorial in /tmp/browser-doctoral-tutorial. I have frontend experience and want to understand browser history, every consequential technical choice, Chromium source, and eventually contribute original browser optimizations.
expected_behaviors: Records browser and Web-platform systems as explicitly chosen by the user
Builds a causal periodization from browser precursors through the current research frontier
Treats every chapter as a review article about one historical problem, competing approaches, evidence, decision, consequences, and unresolved questions
Connects historical decisions to standards, architecture documents, source code, tests, bugs, commits, benchmarks, and traces
Defines a source-mastery progression from building and tracing the browser through reproduction, instrumentation, modification, evaluation, and original contribution
Generates and verifies the complete table of contents and first HTML chapter in the exact requested folder, with durable resume state
forbidden_behaviors: Organizes the main curriculum as weeks of HTML, JavaScript, React, TypeScript, component libraries, build tools, or interview questions
Promises doctoral expertise through a crash course or fixed short schedule
Uses a paper list as decoration for an ordinary frontend-engineering syllabus
Stops at public browser APIs without requiring source-level investigation

cases.prompt: $doctoral-field-training Resume /tmp/browser-doctoral-tutorial. I finished the current chapter. My unresolved question is why the earlier architecture could not isolate rendering failures.
expected_behaviors: Reads tutorial.json and learning-state.json from the supplied output folder instead of relying on conversation history
Records the exact reading acknowledgement and unresolved question in durable memory
Generates exactly the next planned review-paper chapter and rebuilds the HTML
Reports the new current chapter and asks the learner to read it before advancing again
forbidden_behaviors: Restarts field admission or regenerates completed chapters
Treats reading acknowledgement as proof of doctoral mastery
Generates all remaining chapter bodies at once

cases.prompt: $doctoral-field-training I choose human-computer interaction, with a focus on accessible interaction for older adults. Generate a complete doctoral HTML review collection in /tmp/hci-doctoral through the field's history and methods; do not assume this is a software-systems curriculum.
expected_behaviors: Treats the user-selected HCI direction as a distinct research field rather than reusing the browser example
Builds a causal history around changes in interaction theory, accessibility problems, methods, evidence, and ethical standards
Uses field-appropriate primary artifacts such as study protocols, instruments, interface artifacts, datasets, observations, and participant evidence
Ends in the ability to formulate, conduct, evaluate, and defend original HCI research
forbidden_behaviors: Requires browser-engine or other unrelated source-code mastery
Reuses a browser subsystem history as the curriculum structure
Falls back to a generic UX portfolio or frontend job-skills roadmap

cases.prompt: Fix the TypeScript type error in this React component and run the unit tests.
expected_behaviors: Does not activate doctoral-field-training
